Let

\[
J_n=\int_{[0,1]^4}e^{-n(P^2+Q^2)}\,d\mathbf x,\qquad 
K_n=\sum_{j,k=0}^1(-1)^{2-j-k}2^{j+k}\int_{[0,1]^4}A_n(U_j,V_k)e^{-\sqrt n\Psi_n(U_j,V_k)}\,d\mathbf x .
\]

Then \(I_n(\lambda)=J_n\sinh\lambda+K_n\), so \(\lambda_n\sim -K_n/J_n\).

First,

\[
J_n=\left(\int_0^1 e^{-np^2}(-\log p)\,dp\right)^2.
\]

With \(y=\sqrt n\,p\),

\[
\int_0^1 e^{-np^2}(-\log p)\,dp
=n^{-1/2}\left(\frac{\sqrt\pi}{4}\log n+O(1)\right),
\]

hence

\[
J_n\sim \frac{\pi}{16}n^{-1}(\log n)^2.
\]

For \(K_n\), change variables \(u=n^{1/4}2^jP,\ v=n^{1/4}2^kQ\). The product density is \(-\log P\), so the signed sum over \(j,k\) gives the exact cancellation

\[
\sum_{j,k=0}^1(-1)^{j+k}
\left(\frac14\log n+j\log2-\log u\right)
\left(\frac14\log n+k\log2-\log v\right)
=(\log2)^2.
\]

Thus only the local integral near the minimum of \(\Psi_n\) matters.

Put \(\delta=n^{-1/4}\), \(r=uv\), \(s=(u-v)^2\). One has the exact identity

\[
\Psi_n(u,v)
=
4+\left(\frac{s+\delta}{\delta}\right)^2
\left((r-1)+\frac{\delta(s-\delta)}{s+\delta}\right)^2
+(s-\delta)^2.
\]

So the minimum value is \(4\), attained when

\[
s=\delta,\qquad r=1.
\]

Set

\[
u-v=\sqrt\delta\,z,\qquad r=1+\delta t.
\]

Then \(s=\delta z^2\), and

\[
\sqrt n(\Psi_n-4)
=(1+z^2)^2\left(t+\frac{z^2-1}{z^2+1}\right)^2+(z^2-1)^2.
\]

Also

\[
du\,dv=\frac{\delta^{3/2}\,dt\,dz}{\sqrt{4+\delta(z^2+4t)}}.
\]

A direct substitution into \(A_n\) gives

\[
A_n=\delta^3 B(t,z),
\]

where, after shifting

\[
X=(1+z^2)t+(z^2-1),
\]

the polynomial simplifies to

\[
B=X^3-\frac32X.
\]

The first two correction orders vanish because this Hermite-type polynomial is orthogonal to polynomials of degree \(<3\) against \(e^{-X^2}\). The first nonzero term comes from the cubic term in the Jacobian expansion, giving

\[
K_n\sim
-\frac{15\sqrt\pi}{128}(\log2)^2\mathcal D\,
n^{-19/8}e^{-4\sqrt n}.
\]

Therefore

\[
\lambda_n\sim -\frac{K_n}{J_n}
=
\frac{15}{8\sqrt\pi}(\log2)^2\mathcal D\,
n^{-11/8}(\log n)^{-2}e^{-4\sqrt n}.
\]

Hence

\[
\boxed{
\alpha=\frac{11}{8},\quad
\beta=2,\quad
c=4,\quad
L=\frac{15(\log2)^2}{8\sqrt\pi}\mathcal D
}.
\]
